verses.1: He lifted the cover aside, and I saw the treasures hidden there. They were like treasures from the depths of the earth, revealed to me.
verses.2: May those who dwell on the island of Sohar be blessed, far from the sea.
verses.3: And in many waters, black seeds will be sown. Then, at dawn, they will be harvested, and they will become a source of wealth for the nations.
verses.4: Boshi Tzidon said, “The sea is vast and endless.” He also said, “I have never been sick, nor have I ever been born or grown up in any place.” I’ve always lived in caves.
verses.5: When they heard that the Egyptians were approaching, they rushed forward as if they had heard the sound of war.
verses.6: Go through Tarshish; may those who dwell in Ai be destroyed.
verses.7: This is good news for you from ancient times. Its feet were carried far away from its place of origin.
verses.8: Who could advise the builder of this house, whose workers are like slaves who work under cruel conditions?
verses.9: Yehovah, the Almighty, commanded that all cattle be slaughtered, so that all the livestock on earth might be destroyed.
verses.10: Travel through your land like the sun in the midst of its heat; there’s no longer any rest or peace.
verses.11: His hand was stretched out over the sea. The kings of Yahweh commanded that Mawzenyah be destroyed in Kanaan.
verses.12: And he said, “Do not go further into that desolate place where there are only ruins. Go away from there. Even there, do not stay.”
verses.13: And this land of ruins… This people never established any cities there. They built their homes in the wilderness, but their cities were destroyed.
verses.14: May they be blessed, O Tarshish, because Shudad is a proud man.
verses.15: And on that day, the city will be forgotten for seventy years. After that, it will once again become a city, just like the song of the Zonah.
verses.16: Please take a lamp with you. This forgotten city needs light. I can play songs to help you remember.
verses.17: And it shall be that in seventy years, the LORD will destroy Zion, and it will return to its former state. All the kings of the earth will be under his rule on this land.
verses.18: And its grain and its fruits shall be holy to Jehovah. They shall not be used for anything other than food for seven people, and they shall be used as an offering to Jehovah.
